title: XW-ENC-AFFINITY-1 (apex-mf6) L3 live: pinned same-model 2-turn session KEEPS ciphertext on the wire (design 5 pty_e2e first half: 'same-model 2-turn session keeps ciphertext on the wire when pinned'). Fresh ACP session on gpt-5.6-sol, NO switch; config_patch carries ONLY the global [models] default_reasoning_effort='max' (O7 M-1 carrier-mint fix: the session's wire effort resolves from the models-manager current effort, which seeds from that global and projects onto the row menu (xhigh -> model default 'low' on the sol row), so a row-level reasoning_effort scalar CANNOT steer it — attempt 1/2 proved the scalar inert on the wire; the original trivial echo at the projected effort 'low' minted no reasoning/encrypted_content carrier, wave 20260920T072948Z forensics A; the row's x-litellm-tags pin is UNTOUCHED — expected tag 'East US 2'; the wave's live probe settles the live-config premise, an untagged sol row is a REPORT finding, not a case edit). Turn 1 (a reasoning-forcing modular-exponentiation prompt at the strongest expressible effort, tool-free by instruction so the turn-request count stays deterministic) mints: the response's reasoning item is mint-stamped (D1, store-side only) with the sol row's pin. Turn 2's request then replays turn 1's ride through the SEND-TIME gate: pin Some(EU2) x mint Some(EU2) = RETAIN (deterministic same-boundary) -> the encrypted_content CROSSES the second sol request. This is THE mf6 behavioral delta on the pinned path: the retired D-ENC stripped encrypted_content unconditionally at every /responses send, so under pre-mf6 code this pin is ABSENT and REDs. Zero 400/503 by construction (same-boundary retention is the deterministic arm): any retry on a pinned row (turn-request count >2) = a boundary error where none was possible = classification drift -> report-and-stop. Suite is cross-wire (the committed schema has no enc-affinity suite; the affinity semantics live in the pins).

steps.prompt: Find the remainder when 7^8432 is divided by 5557. Work it out by hand using modular exponentiation (repeated squaring), showing each step, without using any tools or code execution.

ndjson.label: BOTH TURNS COMPLETE: no turn error (an ACP error = regression beyond the documented surface -> report-and-stop).

wire.label: L3 PIN-RETAIN (the mf6 delta pin): the second sol request carries the first turn's reasoning ciphertext — D1 mint-stamped the ride with the pinned sol row's tag and the send-time gate (pin Some x mint Some, exact-string N-3) = RETAIN. Absent = a D-ENC-style unconditional strip (pre-mf6 behavior), a missing D1 mint stamp, or the live sol row untagged (premise failure -> the wave's live probe disambiguates; report-and-stop, never a case edit).

TWO TURNS NO RETRY: 2 = one request per turn (same-boundary retention is deterministic — zero 400/503 by construction); 1 = the second turn never fired -> report-and-stop; >2 = a retry class fired on a PINNED row (a boundary error where none was possible = classification drift, e.g. is_enc_boundary_error catching a non-ENC 503) -> report-and-stop. SCOPED (O7/M-1): where adds body.max_output_tokens=128000 (the sol row's max_completion_tokens) to exclude the unconditional first-prompt session-title side call (max_output_tokens=100) — this fork's fast title path is NOT gated by features/turn_summary (the runner comment claiming both side-calls share the gate is stale; title_refresh is gated but the FIRST-PROMPT title is ungated), and wave 20260920T072948Z proved it lands on /v1/responses under the session model on every fresh ACP session (the committed schema's own where description names this artifact, which made the unscoped max=2 unsatisfiable: 3 sol POSTs). The count therefore covers USER-TURN requests only; if the row's max_completion_tokens changes this pin fail-louds (0 matches) — update the scope, never the band.
FINAL ACCEPTED: the final sol request reached 200 (a pinned same-boundary request must never 400/503). Non-200 final = classification drift or new wire-error shape -> report-and-stop.
